claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys have a vast combinatorial composition space because they contain multiple principal elements.
A fast method for screening refractory HEA compositions is currently lacking.
An integrated high-throughput model combining simulation outputs and experimental datasets can rapidly identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
The integrated model will screen compositions more efficiently than traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation-based methods.
A machine-learning model trained on simulation outputs and experimental data can predict strength, ductility, and density.
Standardized computational and experimental conditions will ensure consistent processing parameters during screening.
The integrated dataset can produce predicted composition parameters and associated microstructural indicators.
Patterns learned from prior experimental and simulation data enable rapid prediction of strength, ductility, and density.
Rapid property prediction will narrow the candidate-alloy set to compositions satisfying the design criteria.
Model-selected RHEA compositions will experimentally demonstrate superior strength compared with compositions selected by traditional methods.
Model-selected RHEA compositions will experimentally demonstrate superior ductility compared with compositions selected by traditional methods.
Model-selected RHEA compositions will not have a significant weight increase compared with compositions selected by traditional methods.
Traditional thermo-kinetic analyses and direct simulations without data integration are slower and less efficient at navigating the RHEA composition space.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to refractory HEA systems having ample experimental and simulation data.
Sparse training data may limit the effectiveness of the approach.
The approach may be less effective for non-refractory alloy compositions.
